newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Southeast Asian leaders gather for annual summit.
newsitem.headline: Southeast Asian leaders gather for annual summit.

text.p: Southeast Asian heads of government gathered in Jakarta on Friday on the eve of an "informal" summit expected to cover Burma's bid to join ASEAN and next month's world trade meeting in Singapore.

Indonesia's President Suharto, one of the world's longest serving leaders, is playing host to ASEAN leaders and observers who include active and retired generals, descendants of royalty, communists and the world's richest man.

The leaders of the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations have billed the Jakarta meeting on Saturday as an informal summit. Most of them met last week in Manila for the annual Asian-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Burma, Cambodia and Laos are attending the summit for the first time as observers.
Philippine President Fidel Ramos, like Suharto a former army general, said on arrival on Friday that the timing of granting Burma full ASEAN membership would be one of the issues taken up.

"We have already given that assurance (of admitting Burma)," he told reporters. "But of course, there are certain steps to be undertaken, including (setting up) common effective preferential tariffs."
Diplomats said the leaders were also expected to discuss the inaugural ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation -- the global trade regulatory body -- in Singapore next month.
ASEAN members oppose efforts by the United States and some other Western powers to broaden the WTO agenda to include items such as labour standards and investment guarantees.

Burma's military ruler, General Than Shwe, was already in Jakarta, his presence clouded by the growing speculation on whether his government's crackdown on Nobel peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi's pro-democracy movement could delay Rangoon's acceptance into ASEAN.
Both Laos and Cambodia are to admitted to ASEAN next year but moves to admit Burma have hit a storm of criticism from Western nations and disquiet among some regional leaders.
Ramos and Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong have both questioned whether Rangoon is ready to join ASEAN, but have stressed that the principle of granting full membership is not in doubt.
Than Shwe met with Suharto on Friday and outlined the internal situation in Burma, Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono said.
"The leader of Myanmar (Burma) gave an explanation in general to the president over the things related to Aung San Suu Kyi," Murdiono told reporters after the meeting. He did not elaborate.
Lao Prime Minister General Khamtay Siphandone arrived in Jakarta on Wednesday for a state visit ahead of the summit.

He and Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, who was to arrive later on Friday, are the two communist heads of government to be represented at the summit, which groups some of the world's fastest-growing nations.

Singapore's Goh was also arriving on Friday, along with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and hereditary ruler Sultan Sir Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei, who tops Fortune magazine's list of the world's wealthiest men.

Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan is representing Thailand following general elections there, while Cambodia's first and second prime ministers are also attending -- but arriving separately after public squabbles in recent weeks.
